question: Can a parameterized asymmetric-discovery task bank be certified arithmetically BEFORE freeze — with cold and retrieval-shaped baselines demonstrably below ceiling at high residual novelty (≥0.7), a real treatment/comparator behavioural distinction (SPIDER-inheritance vs retrieval-only vs cold), honest per-condition counters (http_requests, retrieval_calls, verification_calls, repair_attempts), and a preregistered contamination/dynamic-range certificate — delivered as a reusable substrate on the runtime lane path that unblocks blocker B2 for the flagship inheritance benchmark?
hypothesis: A task bank constructed from parameterized web interaction sequences with controlled residual novelty (≥0.7) will yield cold baseline success ≤0.60 and retrieval baseline success ≤0.75 (both with upper 95% Wilson bound <0.85), while a SPIDER-inheritance treatment arm shows a statistically detectable behavioural distinction (Δsuccess ≥0.20, Δcost_ratio ≤0.70) with honest counters, and the dynamic range certificate (ceiling gap ≥0.25 for cold, ≥0.15 for retrieval) is arithmetically verifiable from the frozen task bank parameters alone before any outcome measurement.
falsifier: If the frozen task bank parameters imply cold baseline success >0.75 or retrieval baseline success >0.85 (upper Wilson bound), or if the maximum achievable treatment-comparator Δsuccess <0.15 under the parameterized novelty model, or if honest counter instrumentation cannot be implemented without synthetic fallback, then the task bank cannot serve as a non-degenerate B2 substrate and the design is falsified at the arithmetic certificate stage.

COLD.description: Agent executes task with no prior knowledge, no retrieval, no SPIDER mechanisms — pure exploration from initial state

RETRIEVAL_ONLY.description: Agent receives retrieved trajectory fragments (semantic similarity top-k) but no SPIDER parameterization, verification, or repair — retrieval-shaped comparator per P2-REPLAY-COST guard

positive_control.description: Exact replay of a previously successful trajectory on the same task (zero novelty) — must achieve success=1.0, cost_ratio=1.0 vs first-agent cost, verifying the substrate can detect perfect inheritance when novelty=0
positive_control.expected_behavior: success_rate=1.0, cost_ratio=1.0, http_requests=first_agent_cost, retrieval_calls=0, verification_calls=0, repair_attempts=0

null_control.description: Task parameters shuffled to destroy semantic coherence while preserving surface statistics — must yield success ≤ cold baseline, verifying that any treatment effect requires semantic structure not surface statistics

measurement_validity.authorship_separation: Task bank construction (runtime lane) is separate from SPIDER inheritance mechanism (graph/product lanes). The runtime substrate provides task execution, counter instrumentation, and novelty certification. The inheritance mechanism is injected at EXECUTE via a defined adapter interface.
measurement_validity.counter_instrumentation: All HTTP requests via instrumented transport; retrieval calls via explicit registry lookup API; verification calls via explicit verification API; repair attempts via explicit repair API. No synthetic fallback — missing instrumentation is a measurement failure recorded in validity_notes.
measurement_validity.novelty_certification: Residual novelty computed from task bank parameterization (structural Hamming distance between task graph and nearest known fragment) and certified arithmetically before freeze. The certificate is a pure function of frozen task bank JSON and does not depend on outcome data.
measurement_validity.contamination_controls: Task bank split: certification set (frozen, used for arithmetic certificate) and evaluation set (disjoint, used for outcome measurement). No parameter leakage between sets. Retrieval index built only from certification set for retrieval baseline.
measurement_validity.ceiling_detection: Pre-freeze arithmetic certificate computes theoretical maximum success for cold/retrieval given task bank parameters. If upper Wilson bound ≥0.85 for either baseline, the certificate FAILS and the experiment cannot freeze.

decision_rule.arithmetic_certificate: PASS iff: (1) certified_cold_upper_wilson < 0.85, (2) certified_retrieval_upper_wilson < 0.85, (3) certified_residual_novelty ≥ 0.70, (4) max_theoretical_Δsuccess ≥ 0.20, (5) counter_instrumentation_complete = true. All five must PASS for freeze eligibility.
decision_rule.outcome_rule: After EXECUTE: SUPPORTS iff (a) observed cold success ≤0.65 with upper Wilson <0.80, (b) observed retrieval success ≤0.80 with upper Wilson <0.90, (c) SPIDER treatment Δsuccess ≥0.20 with lower Wilson >0.10, (d) SPIDER treatment cost_ratio ≤0.70, (e) zero counter instrumentation failures, (f) independent recomputation zero_mismatches. FALSIFIES iff any of (a)-(f) fails. MIXED iff certificate PASSES but outcome is INCONCLUSIVE.
decision_rule.promotion_rule: NO claim promotion on arithmetic certificate alone. C-MEAS-VALID and C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY status unchanged until outcome measurement completes with valid SUPPORTS.

product_consequence_positive: B2 blocker resolved: a certified task bank substrate exists with non-ceiling dynamic range, honest counters, and real treatment/comparator distinction. Graph and Product lanes can now preregister the flagship inheritance benchmark (C-LLM-INHERIT/C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY/C-PRODUCT-ECON) using this substrate. The task bank and counter harness are promoted to reusable runtime substrate.
product_consequence_negative: B2 blocker persists: no task bank with certified non-ceiling dynamic range exists. The flagship inheritance benchmark cannot be preregistered with measurement validity. Runtime lane must PARK or PIVOT per Global Director. Graph/Product lanes must either weaken B2 dependency or accept UNKNOWN on inheritance economics.
expected_information_gain: High: resolves the single documented B2 blocker on the critical path. A valid certificate changes the architectural decision from 'benchmark blocked' to 'benchmark preregistrable'. A falsified certificate proves the current task parameterization approach cannot yield non-ceiling baselines, forcing a PIVOT to a different task bank construction strategy.

freeze_eligibility.decision_rule_reachability: PASS: The arithmetic certificate is a pure function of frozen task bank parameters (JSON) and frozen decision thresholds. No outcome data required. The certificate either passes or fails deterministically at DESIGN time.
freeze_eligibility.measurement_prerequisites: PASS: All required components exist or are specified for construction: (1) parameterized task bank generator (new code in research/runtime/task_bank.py), (2) instrumented execution harness (new code in research/runtime/task_harness.py), (3) counter APIs (http, retrieval, verification, repair) defined as abstract interfaces with concrete implementations. No external unavailable dependencies.
freeze_eligibility.baseline_identifiability: PASS: Cold and retrieval baselines are operationally defined (no inheritance vs retrieval-only). Their theoretical ceilings are computable from task bank parameters (graph connectivity, novelty distribution). The Wilson upper bounds are deterministic functions of n and expected p.
freeze_eligibility.control_sensitivity: PASS: Positive control (known route replay) must achieve 1.0 success — any deviation indicates substrate failure. Null control (shuffled novelty) must not exceed cold baseline — any excess indicates surface-statistic confounding. Both are discriminating and executable.
freeze_eligibility.treatment_liveness: PASS: The SPIDER-inheritance treatment is implemented via a defined adapter interface (TaskInheritanceAdapter) that the Graph/Product lanes will provide at EXECUTE. The interface is specified in the frozen design. A stub implementation exists for DESIGN-time certificate validation. The treatment is structurally capable of becoming executable.
freeze_eligibility.freeze_artifacts_bound: PASS: All mutable local dependencies are listed in freeze_artifacts below with exact repository-relative paths. The freezer will hash them into freeze.json.artifact_hashes.
